title: Applied ML Eval Harness: Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization Profiles, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Sana Kapoor
body:
Summary:
This playbook describes Redwood Inference's standard process for onboarding models into the eval harness, curating prompt sets and benchmarks, defining quantization profiles, and operating the regression triage workflow. It is intended for ML engineers, applied ML, and platform engineers responsible for model serving quality and cost/performance tradeoffs.

Goals:
- Ensure consistent, reproducible evaluations for every model we serve.
- Maintain prompt sets and benchmarks that reflect customer workloads and edge cases.
- Define quantization profiles that balance cost and quality per workload.
- Provide a fast, accountable regression triage process when eval or production signals indicate quality regressions.

Scope and audience:
This document applies to: models being onboarded to Redwood Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments; applied-ml team members running evals; platform engineers integrating models into routing/catalog; and SRE/QA teams monitoring regressions.

Quick Links:
- Eval harness standards: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/applied-ml-eval-harness-standards-2025
- Prompt set guidelines: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks-guidelines-2026
- Quantization profiles: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quantization-profiles-best-practices-2026

1) Model onboarding checklist (high-level)
Follow this checklist for every new model/version prior to declaring it ready for production rollout. The checklist is enforced by the eval harness CI pipeline and gated by approvals.

1. Create model entry in model-catalog (PR to catalog repo) with: name, architecture, framework, base checkpoint, supported seq lengths, and known incompatibilities.
2. Assign evaluation owner and primary reviewer (applied-ml).
3. Add baseline prompt sets from verticals: core-nlu, code-assist, summarization, instruction-following, safety-edge-cases. Use the standard naming: <model>-<vertical>-promptset-v1.
4. Configure quantization profile draft (see section 3).
5. Run end-to-end eval harness tests (unit + regression + quality thresholds).
6. Review eval results and sign-off (owner + two reviewers).
7. Schedule staged rollout: internal -> beta customers -> general availability.

2) Eval harness configuration and required outputs
Every eval run must produce machine-readable artifacts that are stored in the eval run S3 bucket and indexed in the eval metadata catalog. Minimum required artifacts:
- results.json (per-prompt metrics)
- summary.csv (aggregated metrics per-vertical)
- diff_report.html (human-readable regression highlights)
- artifacts/ (raw model outputs, token-level logs, RNG seeds)
- config.yaml (evaluation config used)

Example config.yaml (required keys):
```
model_name: sample-model-v1
run_id: onboarding-2027-05-01
owner: sana.kapoor@redwood.ai
verticals:
  - summarization
  - core-nlu
prompt_sets:
  summarization: sample-model-summarization-promptset-v1
  core-nlu: sample-model-core-nlu-promptset-v1
metrics:
  - rouge
  - exact_match
  - toxicity_score
  - latency_ms_p95
quantization_profile: q4_1024_mixed
seed: 42
target_slo:
  latency_p95_ms: 120
  accuracy_delta_pct: -1.5   # allowed drop vs baseline
```

3) Quantization profiles and guidelines
Quantization profiles should be defined per-model and per-workload when feasible. Profiles live in the quantization-profiles directory and use a small YAML manifest with the following fields. The table below summarizes common profile types and typical cost/quality tradeoffs.

Profile manifest required fields (flat YAML):
- profile_name
- precision (q4, q8, fp16)
- KV_cache_support (yes/no)
- expected_token_throughput_rtx6000 (tokens/s)
- fallback_profile (profile_name or none)
- notes

Representative profile table:
| profile_name | precision | expected_cost_delta | expected_quality_delta | notes |
|--------------|-----------|---------------------|------------------------|-------|
| q8_fp16_pref | q8       | -25%                | -0.5%                  | Default for low-cost batch workloads|
| q4_1024_mixed| q4       | -45%                | -2.5%                  | Aggressive quant; good for chat with caching|
| fp16_highacc | fp16     | +5%                 | 0%                     | Highest fidelity, higher cost|

Best practices:
- Start with fp16 for initial onboarding if model supports it, then evaluate q8 and q4 profiles on the same prompt sets.
- Always run quantization regression evals that include both semantic and safety prompt sets.
- If quality drop > 2% absolute on key metric, do not roll out to general traffic without mitigation.

4) Prompt sets and benchmarks: structure and guidelines
Prompt sets are the canonical inputs we use to measure model quality and detect regressions. Structure each prompt set as: metadata header, prompts (with labels), expected outputs (where applicable), scoring function and tags.

Required metadata fields for a prompt set file:
- promptset_name
- vertical
- created_by
- created_at
- version
- sample_count
- tags (list)

Examples of verticals and example considerations:
- core-nlu: slot filling, intent detection, ambiguous queries, low-resource languages.
- code-assist: multi-turn code edits, inline diffs, docstring generation.
- summarization: long-context truncation, faithfulness checks, hallucination probes.
- safety-edge-cases: prompt injections, policy evasion, toxic completions.

Benchmarking cadence and thresholds:
- Onboarding: run full benchmark (all verticals) and record baseline metrics.
- Nightly: run high-priority prompt sets (top 5 verticals) and post to eval dashboard.
- Regression window: retain 90 days of prompt set results for triage and trend analysis.

5) Regression triage playbook (operational steps)
When the eval harness or production monitoring flags a regression (metric change beyond threshold), follow this triage workflow. The aim is to quickly identify root cause, mitigate customer impact, and formalize a fix and regression test.

Triggers (alerts):
- Eval harness: delta vs baseline > configured threshold (absolute or relative) for two consecutive runs.
- Production telemetry: customer error reports, increased safety incidents, or automated quality signals (e.g., ranking NDCG drop).
- Canary/rollout guardrails: degradation in canary cohort compared to control >= configured threshold.

Immediate actions (within 2 hours):
1. Pager/notify applied-ml on-call and model owner.
2. Collect artifacts: results.json, config.yaml, sample raw outputs, and relevant production logs.
3. Run quick-diff job: run new vs baseline on top-50 failing prompts and generate diff_report.html.
4. If regression affects safety signals or severe customer-impact paths, escalate to Reliability and Product.

Diagnosis (next 24 hours):
1. Check for recent changes: model weights, tokenizer updates, quantization profile changes, infra kernel updates, or runtime patches.
2. Re-run evals with: fp16 baseline, current quantized profile, and a no-quantization run (if feasible) to isolate quantization vs model drift.
3. Compare RNG seeds and temperature/decoding settings; ensure identical config when comparing.
4. If related to prompt set changes, revert to prior promptset version and re-evaluate.

Mitigation and rollback
- If root cause is infra/kernel/serving regression: revert to prior runtime build + run smoke checks before releasing.
- If root cause is quantization: switch canary to higher-fidelity profile (e.g., fp16) and schedule re-quant evaluation.
- If root cause is model weights: consider pinning traffic to previous version and initiating hotfix model training or prompt engineering.

Postmortem and prevention (within 7 days)
- Owner files a short incident summary in confluence (linkable) with: timeline, root cause, mitigation steps, and action items.
- Create regression unit tests in the eval harness for the failing prompt(s). Tests are added to the nightly high-priority jobs if the regression affects a critical vertical.
- Update quantization profile docs or model-catalog flags where necessary.

6) Roles and responsibilities
- Evaluation Owner (applied-ml): coordinates onboarding, reviews eval outputs, and owns sign-off for rollout.
- Platform Engineer: ensures eval harness CI, config schema, and artifact storage are operational.
- SRE/On-call: triages alerts from production telemetry and coordinates infra rollbacks.
- Product Safety: reviews safety-related regressions and approves mitigations that impact behavior.

7) Metrics, SLOs and thresholds (examples)
- Latency SLO for interactive chat: p95 <= 120 ms (target depends on model class).
- Allowed accuracy delta vs baseline on onboarding: -1.5% absolute on primary metric for go/no-go.
- Nightly regression alert threshold: relative delta >= 3% on core-nlu exact_match across two runs.
- Quantization allowed quality drop: <= 2% absolute on vertical-specific critical metric (unless otherwise justified).

8) Operational checklists and runbooks (brief)
- Pre-onboarding runbook: validate tokenization, ensure model supports requested sequence lengths, smoke-run inference on internal small dataset.
- Nightly-failure runbook: requeue failing jobs, notify owner, attach artifacts, and increment incident counter in the triage board.
- Rollout abort conditions: any safety regression, or any customer-facing regression detected in beta cohort.

9) Example triage timeline (template)
- T0 (0-15m): alert received, immediate notify + artifact collection.
- T0+2h: quick-diff analysis complete and initial mitigation decision (rollback/canary adjust).
- T0+24h: detailed diagnosis and short-term fix implemented.
- T0+72h: long-term fix plan and scheduled work items assigned.

10) Appendices
A. Eval harness CI commands (examples):
- Trigger a full eval run: 
  ./scripts/run_evals.sh --model sample-model-v1 --config configs/sample-onboarding.yaml
- Run quick diff: 
  ./scripts/quick_diff.sh --baseline runs/baseline-2027-04-01 --candidate runs/onboarding-2027-05-01 --out diff_report.html

B. Artifact retention and storage
- Eval artifacts retained: 365 days for onboarding runs, 90 days for nightly runs (configurable per-project).
- Storage location pattern: s3://redwood-eval-artifacts/<model_name>/<run_id>/

C. Example escalation contact list (primary/backup):
- applied-ml-oncall: applied-ml-oncall@redwood.ai (primary) / applied-ml-backup@redwood.ai (backup)
- platform-oncall: platform-oncall@redwood.ai
- product-safety: product-safety@redwood.ai
